title: Review weak hash
why: MD5 and SHA-1 do not provide modern collision resistance. Their presence is a security-review hotspot, not proof of a vulnerability: a digest may identify non-security data or implement an externally fixed protocol.
suggestion: Determine what the digest protects. Use an appropriate modern primitive for security designs you control. For proven non-security hashing, usedforsecurity=False documents intent without changing digest bytes. For provider-mandated protocols, review and document the constraint rather than replacing the algorithm unilaterally or mislabeling security use as non-security.
limitations: Textual detection recognizes hashlib.md5, hashlib.sha1, and new calls naming MD5 or SHA-1; new receiver identities and imported aliases are not resolved.
The rule does not establish cryptographic purpose, exploitability, protocol ownership, or whether a digest reaches a security-sensitive sink.

Explicit usedforsecurity=False intent is accepted. Filenames, caches, extractor code, HTTP requests, and fixed provider protocols are not blanket exemptions because those shapes can also protect security boundaries.
